info.title: KeyBurn API
info.summary: Zero-knowledge API for self-destructing secrets and secret requests.
info.description:
Every value sent to this API is produced by client-side cryptography (protocol osss/v1): secrets are encrypted on the sender's device with AES-256-GCM, and only ciphertext, sizes and hashes of link-derived tokens reach the server. Links carry their key after '#', which must never be sent to any server, including this one.

AI agents should not call this API directly: use the local osss tool (https://keyburn.dev/agents), which implements the protocol and never prints secrets. The protocol is implemented by the reference client osss (versioned downloads under https://keyburn.dev/cli/, listed in SHA256SUMS) and described at https://keyburn.dev/security.

There is no authentication: possession of a link is the authorization (see https://keyburn.dev/auth.md). Requests from browsers must be same-origin. Limits per client IP: 10 creations, 60 reads and 10 uploads per minute, plus daily quotas.

post.description: Stores an already encrypted secret. `id` must equal the first 16 bytes of SHA-256("osss/v1/secret/bound-id" || metaHash). If `file` is declared, upload its ciphertext with the returned `uploadToken` within 15 minutes.

post.summary: Check a secret without opening it
post.description: Returns whether a secret is still available and whether it needs a passphrase. Does not use a view.
Returns the ciphertext and uses up one view. A wrong passphrase (wrong readToken) returns 403 `wrong_passphrase` with `attemptsLeft`; after 5 the secret is destroyed.

post.summary: Receipt: when a secret was opened
post.description: For the sender, with the manage token from the receipt link.

manageToken.description: The token from the receipt link (/m#<id>.<manageToken>).

post.description: Deletes the content and any file immediately; the receipt remains.

manageToken.description: The token from the receipt link.

post.description: Streams the encrypted file once, using the ticket returned by /secret/open.

post.summary: Create a request for a secret
post.description: Stores a request. `id` must equal the first 16 bytes of SHA-256("osss/v1/request/bound-id" || submitHash). `pub` is the requester's P-256 public key.
Returns the encrypted note while the request is open.
Stores the answer, encrypted to the requester's public key with an ephemeral ECDH key.

post.summary: Inbox: has the request been answered
post.description: For the requester, with the token derived from the inbox link.

inboxToken.description: HKDF(Q || d, "osss/v1/request/inbox") from the inbox link.

post.description: Deletes the request and any answer immediately.
Streams the encrypted file once, using the ticket returned by /request/open.

put.description: Uploads exactly the declared number of ciphertext bytes for a secret or a request answer, within 15 minutes of creating it.

get.description: Returns ok when the API is serving requests. Touches no storage.

Id.description: Record id (16 bytes, base64url). Derived from the link and bound to its hash, so it can't be chosen freely.

Token.description: A 32-byte token (base64url) derived from a link with HKDF-SHA-256, or its SHA-256 hash.

PublicKey.description: Uncompressed P-256 public key (65 bytes, base64url).

Ciphertext.description: AES-256-GCM ciphertext (base64url) of a padded payload: at least 1 KiB plus the 16-byte tag; at most about 64 KiB of plaintext.

Kdf.description: Passphrase key-derivation parameters, or null when there is no passphrase.

size.description: Ciphertext size in bytes: padded file (1 KiB to 25 MiB) plus the 16-byte tag.

ticket.description: One-time download ticket, valid for 15 minutes.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request, or a value that doesn't match its link

Forbidden.description: Cross-site request, or a wrong passphrase (wrong_passphrase, with attemptsLeft)

NotFound.description: Unknown record or wrong token (indistinguishable on purpose)

Limited.description: rate_limited, quota_exceeded or capacity; try again later
